coverage_notes: Exhaustive coverage across foundational design (Harry Beck's original 1933 work and historical sources), core algorithmic theory (octilinear drawing, orthogonal layout, bend minimization, complexity), seminal visualization works (Tufte, Shneiderman, Munzner), contemporary metro map applications (set visualization with MetroSets/EulerView, schematic network maps), graph drawing fundamentals (force-directed, tree layout, dynamic graphs), user studies on readability and perception, and domain applications (biochemical pathways, software architecture, workflow visualization, knowledge maps). Swept across multiple angles: historical development, algorithmic foundations, cognitive/HCI aspects, applications, and recent work (2020+). Deduped across multiple search result pages. Authorities covered: Nöllenburg/Wolff (metro maps), Kobourov (force-directed), Tamassia (orthogonal drawing), Tufte (graphical integrity), Shneiderman (information visualization principles), Munzner (visualization design), Beck (original metro design). Gaps: some paywalled specific ACM CHI papers, some specific application domain papers (e.g., certain biology-specific metro map papers), very recent 2026 work may have limited coverage.

sources.title: A Survey on Computing Schematic Network Maps: The Challenge to Interactivity
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of algorithmic approaches for schematic maps; covers computational complexity, running times, and interactivity challenges. Core reference for metro map layout methods. Published August 2022.

sources.title: MetroSets: Visualizing Sets as Metro Maps
sources.notes: Applies metro map metaphor to set visualization using hypergraph model with 4-step pipeline. Published in IEEE TVCG 27(2):1257-1267 (Feb 2021). Evaluated on readability metrics vs EulerView and LineSets.

sources.title: On the Readability of Abstract Set Visualizations
sources.notes: Empirical evaluation comparing MetroSets, LineSets, EulerView for set visualization tasks. Studied readability scaling with set/element count. Published IEEE TVCG 2021.

sources.title: Metro-Line Crossing Minimization: Hardness, Approximations, and Tractable Cases
sources.notes: Computational complexity analysis of metro map optimization problems. Proves NP-hardness of crossing minimization; provides approximation algorithms. Foundational for understanding metro layout complexity.

sources.title: Towards Data-Driven Multilinear Metro Maps
sources.notes: Extends mixed-integer linear programming approaches to arbitrary edge orientations beyond octolinear; adapts Nöllenburg methods. Published Diagrams 2020. Authors: Soeren Nickel, Martin Nöllenburg.

sources.title: Spring Embedders and Force Directed Graph Drawing Algorithms
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of force-directed algorithms from Tutte (1963) through contemporary scalable methods. Traces spring embedder development; covers aesthetic properties and planar drawing guarantees. Author: Stephen Kobourov.

sources.title: A survey of two-dimensional graph layout techniques for information visualisation
sources.notes: Broad graph layout survey covering topology-driven, attribute-driven, hybrid approaches including force-directed, dimension reduction, multi-level techniques. Authors: Helen Gibson, Joe Faith, Paul Vickers (2013).

sources.title: Towards a Topology-Shape-Metrics Framework for Ortho-Radial Drawings
sources.notes: Extends Tamassia's TSM paradigm to ortho-radial drawings with mixed-integer programming for bend minimization. Published SoCG 2017.

sources.title: Orthogonal Graph Drawing with Constraints: Algorithms and Applications
sources.notes: Comprehensive dissertation on constraint satisfaction in orthogonal drawing; covers TSM paradigm applications with spatial/inequality constraints. Key algorithms for metro map layout.

sources.title: Smooth Orthogonal Drawings of Planar Graphs
sources.notes: Combines orthogonal layout clarity with smooth circular arcs at vertices; bridges orthogonal and Lombardi styles. Relevant to modern metro map aesthetic refinements.

sources.title: Ben Shneiderman's Visual Information-Seeking Mantra: Overview first, zoom and filter, then details on demand
sources.notes: Foundational information visualization principle; core to evaluating metro maps as overview mechanisms for complex networks. Central to InfoVis taxonomy and direct manipulation principles.

sources.title: Tufte's Six Principles of Graphical Integrity
sources.notes: Distillation of Edward Tufte's foundational work on data-ink ratio, chartjunk, graphical integrity, small multiples. Ethical framework for schematic diagram design including metro maps.

sources.title: Harry Beck - Wikipedia
sources.notes: Definitive biographical entry on Harry Beck (1902-1974), designer of 1933 London Underground map. Documents original design rationale: electrical circuit inspiration, topological vs geographic abstraction.

sources.title: Transforming the Tube map: Harry Beck's iconic design
sources.notes: Museum documentation of Beck's design process and impact. Provides historical context for metro map metaphor development.

sources.title: Octilinear Force-Directed Layout with Mental Map Preservation for Schematic Diagrams
sources.notes: Algorithm combining spring embedder forces with octilinear magnetic forces; preserves mental map during layout changes. Demonstrates 50% faster task completion with preserved mental map.

sources.title: A survey on automated metro map layout methods
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of metro map layout algorithms by Martin Nöllenburg. Covers optimization approaches and practical considerations.

sources.title: Edge Bundling in Information Visualization
sources.notes: Foundational work on reducing visual clutter through edge bundling; complements metro map approach for handling dense graphs.

sources.title: Hierarchical clustering for graph visualization
sources.notes: Hierarchical aggregation and edge bundling techniques; related approach to multilevel abstraction in metro maps.

sources.title: A Taxonomy and Survey of Dynamic Graph Visualization
sources.notes: Comprehensive taxonomy of dynamic visualization approaches (animated vs timeline-based). Relevant for temporal aspects of metro map variants. Beck et al., Computer Graphics Forum 2017.

sources.title: Visualizing and Interacting with Geospatial Networks: A Survey and Design Space
sources.notes: Survey of 95 papers on geographic + network visualization. Analyzes integration of geographic and topological information; interaction design space. Authors: Schöttler, Yang, Pfister, Bach.

sources.title: Graph Drawing: Algorithms for the Visualization of Graphs
sources.notes: Foundational textbook covering graph drawing algorithms. Authors: Di Battista, Eades, Tamassia, Tollis (1999). Essential reference for orthogonal and hierarchical layout methods.

sources.title: Planar and Poly-Arc Lombardi Drawings
sources.notes: Introduces smooth k-Lombardi drawings with circular arcs. Aesthetic alternative to orthogonal/octolinear for graph visualization. Duncan & Eppstein.

sources.title: Bend minimization
sources.notes: Overview of bend minimization problem in orthogonal graph drawing. References Tamassia (1987) polynomial-time algorithm and NP-completeness results.

sources.title: User performance and reading strategies for metro maps: An eye tracking study
sources.notes: Empirical study of 40 participants on schematic metro map reading; color-coding effects, complexity, task difficulty. Published Spatial Cognition & Computation 2017.

sources.title: Metro Map Colour-Coding: Effect on Usability in Route Tracing
sources.notes: Empirical evaluation showing color importance in reducing cognitive load for route-finding on metro maps.

sources.title: Shape-Guided Mixed Metro Map Layout
sources.notes: Recent work (March 2023) on metro/transit map design with shape constraints. Published Computer Graphics Forum.

sources.title: Cartographic Generalization - Making Effective Maps
sources.notes: Foundational cartography principles of simplification, smoothing, grouping, classification relevant to metro map design as map abstraction.

sources.title: Visualizing ordered bivariate data on node-link diagrams
sources.notes: Evaluation of node-link diagram effectiveness for various task types; aesthetic factors (edge crossings, angular resolution) impact readability.

sources.title: Practical Guidelines for the Readability of IT-architecture Diagrams
sources.notes: HCI perspective on schematic diagram readability and cognitive load; applicable to metro maps as information architecture tools.

sources.title: Aesthetics and automatic layout of UML class diagrams
sources.notes: Application of graph layout algorithms to software architecture diagrams; hierarchical and orthogonal approaches.

sources.title: Concept Maps: Integrating Knowledge and Information Visualization
sources.notes: Theory of concept maps as knowledge visualization; connection to metro map metaphor for abstract domain mapping.

sources.title: Pathway Tools Visualization of Organism-Scale Metabolic Networks
sources.notes: Application of network visualization to biochemical pathways; demonstrates metro map metaphor utility in scientific visualization.

sources.title: Metabopolis: scalable network layout for biological pathway diagrams in urban map style
sources.notes: Direct application of metro/city map metaphor to metabolic pathway visualization. Urban grid-like layout for biological networks. BMC Bioinformatics 2019.

sources.title: Designing complex network visualisations using the wayfinding map metaphor
sources.notes: Contemporary work (2024) on applying map metaphor to network exploration; wayfinding principles for visualization design.

sources.title: Structure Based Aesthetics and Support of Cognitive Tasks for Graph Evaluation
sources.notes: Empirical study of how graph aesthetics (crossings, symmetry, etc.) support cognitive task performance.

sources.title: Perception of Symmetries in Drawings of Graphs
sources.notes: Visual perception research on how symmetries are perceived in graph layouts; paradox that perceived vs actual crossings differ.

sources.title: PREVis: Perceived Readability Evaluation for Visualizations
sources.notes: Recent (2024) framework for evaluating perceived readability of visualizations; methodologically relevant to metro map evaluation.

sources.title: Treebar Maps: Schematic Representation of Networks at Scale
sources.notes: Recent approach (2023) to metro map visualization of large networks; hierarchical representation at scale.

sources.title: Automated Label Placement on Maps via Large Language Models
sources.notes: Contemporary (2025) work on map annotation; addresses practical challenge of labeling schematic maps with LLM-guided placement.

sources.title: The influence of landmark visualization style on task performance, visual attention, and spatial learning in a real-world navigation task
sources.notes: Recent (2024) study on landmark-based navigation; abstract vs realistic representations in wayfinding aids.

sources.title: Fáry's theorem
sources.notes: Foundational theorem: any planar graph can be straight-line drawn without crossings. Establishes theoretical basis for metro map feasibility.

sources.title: Sugiyama Framework for Hierarchical Graph Drawing
sources.notes: Foundational hierarchical layout algorithm (Sugiyama, Tagawa, Toda 1981); 4-phase approach: cycle removal, layer assignment, crossing reduction, coordinate assignment.

sources.title: Scalability of Network Visualisation from a Cognitive Load Perspective
sources.notes: Framework for evaluating how graph visualizations scale with cognitive load; relevant to metro map complexity limits.

sources.title: A Survey on Graph Drawing Beyond Planarity
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of non-planar graph drawing techniques; extends Fáry and planarity-based approaches.

sources.title: HOTVis: Higher-Order Time-Aware Visualisation of Dynamic Graphs
sources.notes: Contemporary approach to temporal graph visualization; relevant for metro map variants with time-varying networks.

sources.title: Visual Abstraction
sources.notes: Theoretical framework for visual abstraction in information visualization; foundational for understanding metro maps as abstractions.

sources.title: What is Topological Mapping?
sources.notes: Application perspective: topological vs metric maps in robotics/navigation; demonstrates utility of topology-only representation.

sources.title: Information cartography in association rule mining
sources.notes: Novel application of cartographic principles to data mining visualization.

sources.title: Network Topology & Visualization Made Simple with Auvik
sources.notes: Practitioner perspective on real-world network topology visualization tools; documents industry application of simplified network diagrams.

sources.title: The City Metaphor in Software Visualization
sources.notes: Related metaphor approach (city = codebase structure); demonstrates broader value of spatial/geographic metaphors for abstract information.

sources.title: SArF Map: Visualizing Software Architecture from Feature and Layer Viewpoints
sources.notes: Application of visualization techniques to software architecture; layered/feature viewpoints related to metro line concepts.
